problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a circuit for its fleet of autonomous drones to inspect nine critical communication towers. The towers are positioned at the following grid coordinates (measured in kilometers relative to a central hub):

Tower Alpha: (59,93)
Tower Beta: (18,152)
Tower Gamma: (36,53)
Tower Delta: (0,52)
Tower Epsilon: (168,172)
Tower Zeta: (187,31)
Tower Eta: (191,1)
Tower Theta: (75,94)
Tower Iota: (176,6)

The flight distances between towers, calculated for optimal energy consumption, are as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 46.1 km
Alpha to Delta: 71.8 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 134.6 km
Alpha to Zeta: 142.2 km
Alpha to Eta: 160.9 km
Alpha to Theta: 16.0 km
Alpha to Iota: 145.8 km
Beta to Gamma: 100.6 km
Beta to Delta: 101.6 km
Beta to Epsilon: 151.3 km
Beta to Zeta: 207.9 km
Beta to Eta: 229.6 km
Beta to Theta: 81.3 km
Beta to Iota: 215.1 km
Gamma to Delta: 36.0 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 177.7 km
Gamma to Zeta: 152.6 km
Gamma to Eta: 163.5 km
Gamma to Theta: 56.6 km
Gamma to Iota: 147.7 km
Delta to Epsilon: 206.5 km
Delta to Zeta: 188.2 km
Delta to Eta: 197.7 km
Delta to Theta: 86.0 km
Delta to Iota: 181.9 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 142.3 km
Epsilon to Eta: 172.5 km
Epsilon to Theta: 121.4 km
Epsilon to Iota: 166.2 km
Zeta to Eta: 30.3 km
Zeta to Theta: 128.5 km
Zeta to Iota: 27.3 km
Eta to Theta: 148.7 km
Eta to Iota: 15.8 km
Theta to Iota: 134.0 km

Due to a signal interference zone, a direct flight path between Tower Alpha and Tower Beta is strictly prohibited. Furthermore, the routing protocol mandates that exactly one of two specific critical links must be incorporated into the inspection loop: either the connection between Tower Beta and Tower Gamma, or the connection between Tower Gamma and Tower Delta.

The objective is to determine the most energy-efficient closed-loop flight path that visits each tower precisely once before returning to the point of origin.
